route_b.method: scanned every RIP-relative LEA in Engine.dll whose target lies in 0x4213c0..0x421490, independent of what follows
route_b.finding: The three hits at 0x18c5xx belong to a subsystem structure at 0x421450 with a count at 0x421580 and a pointer array at 0x421480. None of them stores to 0x421428.

route_a.method: grouped all 7691 DIR64 relocation targets into runs to recover pointer tables, then tested the largest candidate table for references to the slot
route_a.result: none of the 132 entry functions contains any reference to 0x421428; the table is a thunk/dispatch table rather than a static initialiser list

slot_semantics_confirmed.evidence: 0x256f0 does mov rax,[0x180421428]; mov rdx,[rax+0x1F8]; mov rcx,[rdx+0xC0]; call [rax+8]
slot_semantics_confirmed.meaning: the slot is an engine root object; it is dereferenced and dispatched virtually, exactly as 0x90ae0 does with call [rax+0x18]

exhausted: all x86-64 store encodings to a fixed absolute address: RIP-relative qword/dword/byte/immediate, XMM 16-byte, disp32 with and without SIB, unaligned stores whose range covers the slot, LEA-then-store, block-wide immediates
loader relocation application (7691 DIR64 entries, none covering the block)
the accessor route (route B): only three subsystems take the address, none writes the slot
the static-initialiser route (route A): the candidate table is a dispatch table, not initialisers
verdict: With the evidence gathered, the store that publishes Engine.dll+0x421428 does not exist in the static code of Engine.dll, Game.dll or Direct3D11.dll, and it does not happen during the observable part of a running session. It must occur during process or module start-up in a way the current static and attach-based methods cannot capture.
not_proven: that the store is in a fourth module
that start-up ordering alone explains it
that the client cannot be instrumented at creation time
next_options: arm before the first instruction via a start-up hook that does not require HKLM (not identified yet)
